items.reported: Out-of-zip address is rejected instead of redirected
items.correctState: An address that resolves outside the shown zip offers to switch to the zip it does resolve to.
items.checkResult: PASS
items.resolution: The blocker was right that the evidence existed and wrong about where. `locateAddressInZip` puts the ZIP INTO the geocoder query, so an address one ZIP over cannot match and returns exactly like a bad address — and `parseCensusPoint` read the coordinates and dropped `addressComponents.zip`, which the response has always carried. `zipThisAddressResolvesTo` re-asks the same geocoder WITHOUT the ZIP constraint, on the failure branch only and only with a house number, so nothing extra leaves this product on the happy path. The same ZIP back is not a redirect and offers nothing. The switch is OFFERED and never taken automatically: a reader looking at one ZIP's ballot who is silently moved to another has had their question changed for them.
items.verification: Six tests, three seeded — the next-ZIP case, the same-ZIP non-redirect, and the street-only path proving no extra address is geocoded. The reader-facing offer is wired through components/ballot/ballot-narrowing.tsx to /ballot?zip=. NOT re-verified on the rendered DOM: reaching it needs a real out-of-zip address typed against a live geocoder, which the unit seam covers deterministically and a walk would not.
